objective: Associate the brand with extreme human performance through a real scientific and engineering mission.
businessContext: The project required years of technical development, testing and risk management before a high-altitude jump.
strategy: Create the event and scientific project that the brand wanted audiences to experience rather than merely depicting it in an advertisement.
outcomes: The mission completed a high-altitude supersonic freefall and produced equipment, protocols and research documented by the Smithsonian.
whatWorked: The branded promise was enacted through a difficult real-world achievement.
The project created durable content and earned attention.
whatFailed: Mission achievement does not by itself establish incremental product sales.
transferConditions: The organization possesses exceptional operational capability, safety governance and a direct brand connection to the feat.
nonTransferConditions: Do not imitate high-risk spectacle when the brand cannot credibly own or safely execute it.
